title: Journey Signatures — lightweight per-user personalization prototype
content:
TL;DR:
Build a tiny, privacy-friendly per-user "journey signature" that captures high-signal personalization cues (tone, domain affinities, short persistent preferences) in a compact blob that can be appended or applied as a delta to prompts at inference time. Goal is meaningful UX personalization with <5% token overhead and minimal latency impact.

Context / motivation:
- Many product teams want persistent personalization (user tone, product preferences, common entities) but storing full session histories or large profiles is expensive and risky.
- We can often get most of the benefit from a small, canonical representation (a signature) instead of replaying long context.
- This should be compatible with Redwood Hosted + Dedicated + Private: same API surface, different storage/backing (hosted KVS vs customer-managed store).

Key idea:
- Compute a short canonical signature per user (or per journey) comprised of ~3–8 labeled attributes (free-form short strings + small affinity scores) plus a compact fingerprint for context matching. The signature size target is 256–1024 bytes.
- At inference: retrieve signature, apply lightweight transformation (prepend a 1–3 sentence personalization primer or add discrete control tokens) before sending to the model.
- Use TTLs and smoothing to keep signatures current and avoid stale personalization.

Primary product goals (MVP):
1) Deliver measurable improvement in QA/goal-conversion for personalized assistants (target +6–12% relative).
2) Keep extra token cost <5% for common interactions.
3) Latency P95 delta <= 10ms (including KVS lookup + transformation).
4) Opt-in by default per privacy guidance; robust controls for customers in Private mode.

Success metrics / instrumentation:
- Engagement lift: change in user completion rate / task success (A/B).
- Token delta: median additional generated tokens and cost change per request.
- Latency: added time for retrieval and transformation (P50/P95/P99).
- Signature churn: update rate per user (useful for GC policies).
- Privacy incidence: number of compliance requests or flagged artifacts.

User stories:
- As an end user, I want the assistant to remember my preferred writing tone (concise vs. friendly) across sessions, so I don't have to repeat it.
- As a product manager, I want to enable per-user recommendations without holding full chat histories, so we reduce storage cost and compliance surface.
- As an SRE, I need a small, cacheable read pattern with fallbacks to keep 95th latency low under load.
- As a platform integrator, I want the same API to work whether the customer is on Hosted or Private (different storage backends but same behavior).

MVP shape / wireframe:
- Signature schema (textual proto, small):
  - persona_tone: short tag or 1-line example ("formal", "playful", or "Write like a concise product manager")
  - domain_affinities: 1–3 short tokens ("finance", "engineering")
  - sticky_entities: up to 3 canonical entity names (customer orgs, project names)
  - affinity_scores: tiny floats as text ("finance:0.8")
  - created_at, last_update, ttl_hint (for eviction)
  - optional provenance: e.g., "inferred_from: last-10-queries"
- Serving flow (MVP):
  1) Request arrives with user_id or session_token.
  2) Fast KVS lookup (in-memory edge cache; fallback to regional store).
  3) If signature present and not expired, run a deterministic transform to generate short instruction snippet (3–30 tokens).
  4) Prepend snippet to prompt with a strict token budget.
  5) Observe output and update signature async if signals indicate new preferences.

API prototype (subjective format):
- GET /v1/users/{id}/journey_signature -> returns signature blob (etag, ttl_hint, content)
- POST /v1/users/{id}/journey_signature -> upsert a signature (used by ingestion or admin)
- Transform is local library (node/py/rust) that turns blob -> prompt primer; library exposes deterministic summarizer and a sanitizer.

Storage/backing options:
- Hosted: managed regional KV (encrypted at rest), 90-day default TTL, edge caches in 3 regions.
- Dedicated: same but on reserved capacity instance.
- Private: shim to customer KMS/KV or S3-based store with envelope encryption.

Privacy & compliance considerations:
- Avoid storing PII unless explicitly allowed; signatures should prefer abstractions and canonical names over raw user content.
- Default opt-in/off: product-level decision. For Hosted: opt-in required for retention >30 days. For Private: surface configuration to tenant.
- Provide export/delete endpoints and audit logs for signature changes.
- Consider differential privacy/noise on affinity scores for analytics.

Operational concerns:
- Read-heavy: ensure hot users served from edge cache; cold users fetch from regional store. Cache invalidation policy on update.
- Rollback: model can fall back to no-signature mode if KVS errors or latency spikes.
- Cost: profiling—KVS reads per request vs token cost saved by avoiding longer replayed history.

A/B experiment plan:
- Start with assistant-reply tasks where personalization is expected (e.g., email reply drafting, knowledge assistant).
- 5% rollout to target cohort, 25% control, measure success metrics over 4 weeks.
- Safety net: automatic disable if error rate, latency, or cost exceed thresholds.

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- How deterministic should the transform be vs. allowing model-facing soft cues? (deterministic = reproducible, easier testing; soft cues = potentially richer but unpredictable)
- Storage format: JSON text vs compressed binary? JSON is debuggable but bigger. Consider CBOR for private installs.
- TTL heuristics: LRU vs activity-based. What is a sensible default? 30d? 90d?
- How to evaluate personalization quality rapidly? Need small labeled eval set and human ratings.
- Interaction with function-calling / tool use: do we inject signature into system prompt only, or annotate function args?
- Cost accounting: should signature reads be charged separately or included in request unit?

Implementation milestones (rough):
- Week 0–2: prototype local transform library + sample signature encoder/decoder.
- Week 3–5: hosted KVS prototype + edge cache shim; implement GET/POST APIs.
- Week 6–8: integrate with assistant demo surface; run internal manual tests.
- Week 9–12: small external A/B; iterate.

Acceptance criteria for initial rollout:
- Transform latency + KVS read adds <= 10ms P95 for the assistant endpoint under 80th percentile load.
- Token overhead median <= 4% across sampled conversations.
- A/B shows non-negative impact on primary task success with initial signal of engagement lift.

Immediate TODOs (actionable):
- [ ] Spin up minimal prototype library and add unit tests (owner: Dominic). Linked PR skeleton: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prototypes/pull/78
- [ ] Create RFC in Confluence summarizing privacy model (owner: Maya). Ticket: CONF-journey-signatures-1
- [ ] Create JIRA epic and tickets for KVS infra & SDK (owner: Ethan). Starter ticket: JIRA-RK-4567
- [ ] Mock evaluation set for 3 verticals (email, sales, engineering docs) and recruit 6 raters.

Notes to self / brainstorm fragments:
- Maybe allow per-organization "signature templates" so products can ship curated primers instead of free-form inference for enterprise customers.
- Could also use signatures as routing keys to get model variants or specialty quantizations (e.g., finance->use model with finance fine-tune).
- Think about composition: per-user signature + per-device signature + ephemeral session deltas. How to merge? Last-writer-wins or merge heuristic?

Appendix: quick thought examples (how primer might look)
- persona_tone: "Be concise and focus on next steps."
- domain_affinities: "engineering,cli"
- primer (auto-generated): "User prefers concise, action-oriented replies. They often reference 'DeployBot' and like code snippets. Prefer short bullet lists for step-by-step."

Longer-term wishlist (post-MVP):
- Signature diffing to show customers what changed (audit).
- Cross-device sync with conflict resolution.
- Gradient-based auto-updates from model signals (with privacy-safe aggregation).

End of doc.

Meta: this is intentionally rough; the goal is to capture constraints and shape an MVP for quick prototyping. Keep it light and iteratively refine after the prototype demo.
